content.title: RANDOM HOUSEHOLD FIXES THAT WORK BETTER THAN YOU'D EXPECT
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow 1 teaspoon of sugar, dry, without water. It resets the nerve causing the spasm.
**Bad Breath Fast** – Chew on a sprig of fresh parsley for 1 minute to neutralize sulfur compounds.
**Stuffy Nose** – Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth and press a finger between your eyebrows for 20 seconds, it loosens sinus pressure.
**Minor Burns** – Hold the area under cool (not icy) running water for 10 minutes, then dab on plain honey to calm the skin.
**Leg Cramp at Night** – Pinch your upper lip hard for 30 seconds, it can interrupt the nerve signal causing the spasm.
**Splinter Removal** – Soak the spot in warm water with 1 tbsp baking soda for 10 minutes, it helps the splinter rise to the surface.
**Toothache Ache** – Press a small piece of raw garlic against the sore tooth, its natural compounds act as a mild numbing agent.
**Dry, Cracked Heels** – Rub a slice of raw potato over the area before bed, then cover with socks overnight.
**Sore Throat Scratch** – Gargle warm water with 1 tsp salt every few hours to pull swelling out of the tissue.
**Bug Bite Itch** – Press a hot spoon (dipped in hot water) onto the bite for 10 seconds, heat breaks down the itch-causing proteins.
**Follow along** – for more quick, kitchen-tested fixes like this.
content.caption:
A few of these actually have real science behind them. That sugar trick for hiccups works because the granules stimulate the vagus nerve, interrupting the diaphragm spasm that causes hiccups in the first place. The garlic trick for a toothache isn't a myth either, garlic contains allicin, a compound with natural antibacterial and mild numbing properties that can take the edge off pain while you wait to see a dentist. And that hot spoon method for bug bites works because heat denatures the proteins your body reacts to, which is literally what causes the itching signal to your brain. These are small, low-risk tricks, but everyone's body responds a little differently, so take it slow and stop if anything feels off.
